'''''Forsythia koreana''''', commonly called '''gaenari''' ([[Hangul]]: 개나리) or '''Korean goldenbell tree''',<ref name="KNA">{{Cite book|url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|title=English Names for Korean Native Plants|publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]]|year=2015|isbn=978-89-97450-98-5|location=Pocheon|pages=471|access-date=6 June 2017|via=[[Korea Forest Service]]|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf|archivedate=25 May 2017}}</ref> is a [[species]] in the olive family, [[Oleaceae]]. It grows to about {{convert|3|m|ft|abbr=on}}. The leaves are oval in shape, have teeth, and are {{convert|3-12|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. The front of the leaf is dark green and the back is dark blue, but both sides are hairless.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.treesandshrubsonline.org/articles/forsythia/forsythia-koreana/ |title= Forsythia koreana (Redh.)
